final_message: **Status:** Reproduced (on c1caacd; also on published 7.0.5, not on 7.0.4) **Expected:** A browser navigation to `/test` (`Accept: text/html,...`, `Sec-Fetch-Dest: document`) should fall back to `index.html`. **Actual:** It returns `200 text/javascript` with the transformed contents of `test.js`. **Trigger:** The project root has `index.html` and `test.js`, and the browser navigates to the extensionless URL `/test`. **Run:** `pnpm vitest run packages/vite/src/node/server/__tests__/htmlFallbackSourceFile.spec.ts` (needs `pnpm install` first; the test imports from source, so no build is needed.) **Reliability:** Deterministic. The test failed 5 of 5 runs. The `/` sanity check passes. What the patch adds: - A fixture `packages/vite/src/node/server/__tests__/fixtures/html-fallback-source-file/` with `index.html` (containing `click me`) and `test.js`. - A test `htmlFallbackSourceFile.spec.ts` that starts a dev server on that fixture and sends `GET /test` with Chrome's navigation headers. It fails with `expected 'text/javascript' to match /text\/html/`. Version check: I ran the same fixture and headers against the published packages from npm, requesting `/test` twice each time to cover the cached path. - vite 7.0.4: `text/html`, `index.html`, both requests. - vite 7.0.5: `text/javascript`, `test.js`, both requests. This confirms the regression window in the report. Likely cause (pointer only): `isJSRequest('/test')` is true for extensionless paths, so `transformMiddleware` handles the request before the HTML fallback runs. In 7.0.4's built output, `transformMiddleware` passed `html: req.headers.accept?.includes("text/html")` to `transformRequest`. That option is gone from `packages/vite/src/node/server/middlewares/transform.ts` at HEAD, which fits the report's pointer to #20376. No production code was changed.
